# AI Agents for Finance: Controls, Privacy and Deployment Guide

A practical guide to using AI agents in finance workflows with human approval, auditability, data minimization and India privacy context.

## Direct answer

Finance workflows can involve personal data, account actions and high-impact decisions, so human approval and auditability matter more than autonomy. Use agents first for bounded assistance such as summarization, reconciliation preparation, knowledge retrieval or drafting, and keep sensitive actions behind explicit authorization. In India, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act has a staged commencement timeline, so teams should verify which provisions apply on the deployment date and obtain legal advice for regulated use cases.

## When this page is useful

Use this page to build a shortlist or implementation plan, not as a substitute for a vendor contract, security review or hands-on pilot. Compare the same workflow across candidates, keep the evidence date visible, and prefer reversible tests before production access is granted.

## Practical decision checklist

1. Define the exact job the agent must complete and the human owner of the workflow.
2. Verify current plan limits, usage billing and availability directly with the vendor.
3. Grant the smallest repository, API, account and data permissions needed for the pilot.
4. Test failure handling, retries, logging, escalation and rollback before allowing consequential actions.
5. Record the evidence date and re-verify material claims when pricing, models or product capabilities change.
6. For personal or regulated data, evaluate the applicable legal and contractual requirements for the actual deployment; this page is not legal advice.

A verification-first comparison of free or no-cost entry points for AI coding tools, with clear limits and upgrade considerations.

Several coding-agent products provide a no-cost entry point, but “free” does not mean unlimited. GitHub currently offers Copilot Free with usage limits. Current GitHub Copilot individual plan pricing and AI-credit model, with practical notes for developers evaluating paid tiers.

## Direct answer

GitHub's current individual lineup lists Copilot Free at $0, Pro at $10 per month, Pro+ at $39 per month, and Max at $100 per month. GitHub also describes AI Credits as the metered unit used by chat and agent features, while code completions remain outside that credit meter on paid plans. An evidence-backed review of Flowise as an open-source platform for visual AI agents, chatflows and agentflows.

## Direct answer

Flowise describes itself as an open-source generative-AI development platform for building AI agents and LLM workflows. Its official documentation lists three visual builders—Assistant, Chatflow and Agentflow—and platform capabilities such as tracing, analytics, evaluations, human-in-the-loop controls, APIs, CLI/SDK access and workspaces.
